title: Chance that a plasma pool holds an infected donation (log scale)
description: Bar chart on a logarithmic scale of the chance, in per cent, that a pool contains at least one infected donation when, by an invented rate, one donation in 10,000 carries a virus no test can find: computed as 1 − (1 − 1/10,000) to the power of the pool size. One donation, 0.01 per cent; a cryoprecipitate pool of 15, 0.15 per cent; a concentrate pool of 1,000, 9.5 per cent; 5,000, 39 per cent; 20,000, 86 per cent; 30,000, 95 per cent. Pool sizes from the Institute of Medicine (1995) and the Infected Blood Inquiry (2024); the arithmetic is the reading's own.
heading: ONE DONATION IN 10,000 INFECTED (INVENTED) · LOG SCALE
